title: 008-runtime-error-monitoring
universal_lens: The runtime monitoring architecture is modeled as a continuous-time Markov jump process over distributed serverless instances. The transition from an unhandled exception state to an aggregated observability state requires a non-linear projection operator that strictly enforces PII nullification, mapping high-dimensional error manifolds into a secure, low-dimensional diagnostic subspace.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the raw stream of unhandled exceptions acts as a high-frequency stochastic point process. We apply conformal inference to establish dynamic prediction intervals for error spikes across Vercel edge nodes, while the scrubbing protocol functions as a strict Bayesian censoring mechanism, ensuring sensitive priors (PII) are permanently excised before posterior aggregation.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the system operates as a discrete event simulation where route handlers represent fragile tactical states. A checkout failure triggers a catastrophic state-transition; the proposed webhook pipeline serves as a rapid feedback loop, allowing the central control plane to execute emergency recovery maneuvers and prevent cascading systemic collapse.

primitives.name: Observability Gap Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Unhandled route handler exceptions (e.g., checkout 500 at 02:14) are invisible until logs are manually inspected
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{O}: Observation event (dimensionless), \mathcal{E}: Exception occurrence (dimensionless), \lambda_{poll}: Polling frequency (s^-1), t: Time (s)
primitives.assumptions: Polling interval is significantly larger than the mean time between exceptions; manual inspection introduces a heavy-tailed delay distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the exception rate exceeds the polling frequency (\lambda_{error} > \lambda_{poll}), leading to complete information loss.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE blind-spot mechanics where off-ball defensive rotations fail to register due to sensor latency.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-detection delta (seconds) between exception throw and log ingestion.

primitives.name: PII Scrubbing Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Scrub before transmission:** - URLs (strip query params with PII) - Error messages (check for embedded secrets) 3.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Psi_{raw}: Raw error payload vector (dimensionless), \mathcal{K}_{nullify}: Orthogonal projection operator (dimensionless), \phi_{secret}: Secret basis vectors (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: The set of all possible PII patterns \mathcal{S}_{PII} can be approximated by a finite set of regex-based basis vectors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if an adversary encodes secrets using steganographic techniques outside the defined basis \mathcal{S}_{PII}, causing leakage.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI data sanitization pipelines that strip player biometric identifiers before public API broadcasting.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of characters redacted per error payload; false-negative rate of secret detection.

primitives.name: Webhook Feedback Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: context (headers, bodies, user data). The monitoring solution must not leak sensitive data. ## Decision Options
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathbf{x}: System state vector (dimensionless), \mathbf{A}: Intrinsic dynamics matrix (s^-1), \mathbf{B}: Control input matrix (dimensionless), \mathcal{W}: Webhook transmission operator (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: The webhook transmission delay is negligible compared to the timescale of state degradation; the scrubbing kernel is perfectly accurate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System instability arises if the webhook introduces positive feedback loops or if network partitions cause delayed control signals.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSE real-time coaching adjustments based on sanitized telemetry feeds during live gameplay.
layer2.telemetry: Latency from error capture to Slack/Discord notification (ms); throughput of the webhook endpoint (req/s).

The derivation begins by formalizing the 'Context' gap: existing observability relies on scheduled polls, mathematically represented as a low-pass filter that aliases high-frequency runtime exceptions. This creates an information vacuum where critical state transitions (e.g., checkout failures) remain unobserved. To resolve this, we introduce a continuous monitoring operator. However, the introduction of a global error boundary in a distributed serverless environment (Vercel) necessitates a rigorous treatment of data privacy. The 'Security consideration' dictates that any observable \Psi drawn from the high-dimensional state space must undergo a strict projection via the PII Scrubbing Kernel \mathcal{K}_{nullify}. This kernel acts as a mathematical sieve, ensuring the inner product with any secret basis vector is exactly zero. The recommended 'Option 3' constructs a minimal viable feedback loop. By routing the scrubbed error state through a controlled webhook, we establish a closed-loop control system. The dualities here lie between completeness of context (needing headers/bodies for debugging) and security (needing them stripped). The failure mode is a trade-off surface: overly aggressive scrubbing destroys diagnostic utility, while insufficient scrubbing breaches compliance. The derived primitives map these tensions into quantifiable operators, allowing us to model the system's resilience against both technical faults and adversarial data extraction.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two primary agents: the 'Operator' seeking maximum diagnostic entropy to rapidly patch vulnerabilities, and the 'Adversary' attempting to reconstruct sensitive user data from error payloads. The Hermes Agent acts as a neutral arbiter, designing a protocol that satisfies the Operator's need for visibility while imposing hard constraints that frustrate the Adversary's reconstruction attempts, effectively playing a minimax game over the information content of the logs.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A veto is triggered if the scrubbing kernel fails to maintain orthogonality against newly discovered PII patterns, resulting in a collinearity breach between the diagnostic signal and sensitive data. Furthermore, if the webhook feedback loop introduces latency greater than the Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR) threshold, the primitive is vetoed as it provides stale state information, rendering the situational reasoning layer ineffective during active incidents.
